title: Private jet charter to Sri Lanka: permits and rules
description: Private flights to Sri Lanka: landing and overflight permission from the CAASL, lead times and how requests are made, from the Sri Lanka AIP.
h1: Private flights to and from Sri Lanka
lead: Every private or charter flight to Sri Lanka needs the authority's permission first. What the rules are, how far ahead to plan, and what they mean for your trip.

p: The authority is the {{lk.authority}}. The rule for private and charter flights: {{lk.permit}}. A practical point: {{lk.notable}}, which helps when a schedule changes late.

Flights that only cross Sri Lanka's airspace on the way to somewhere else need permission too: {{lk.overflight}}. On routes between the Gulf and South-East Asia this applies more often than travellers expect.

Because both landing and overflight need permission ahead, the schedule has to be fixed earlier than in some other countries. We tell you when the operator needs your final times and passenger details.

The operator that flies your trip applies, usually through its handling agent or a flight-permit service. You do not need to deal with the authority yourself. What you can do is give us final names, passport details and times early, because a permit is issued for a given aircraft, schedule and passenger list, and late changes can mean a new application.

sections.h: How we plan a private flight to or from Sri Lanka
p: Tell us where you are flying from or to, when, and how many people are travelling. We find aircraft from licensed operators, check each operator against our safety standard before you see a quote, and ask the operator to apply for the permits early, because the authority's answer decides the schedule. Any aircraft, any route, upon availability.
Permit rules change. The operator and its handling agent confirm the current rules for your flight before departure; every fact on this page shows its official source and the date we checked it.

faq.q: How far ahead is landing permission needed for Sri Lanka?
Does Archē Executive operate the flight?
faq.a: No. We are a broker. A licensed operator flies every trip, and it is named in your quote and charter agreement before you confirm.
